subject: Logic
title: Appeal to Ignorance
description: A fast breakdown of Appeal to Ignorance for builders.

hook.text: "No one has proven ghosts don't exist—so they must be real." That's not how proof works.

buildup.text: Appeal to ignorance claims something is true because it hasn't been proven false, or vice versa.

discovery.text: Absence of evidence isn't evidence of absence—but it's not evidence of presence either.

twist.text: Before germ theory, nobody had proven germs existed. That didn't mean they weren't there.

climax.text: A lack of disproof means we don't know yet. It doesn't settle the question either way.

quiz.question: What does the appeal to ignorance exploit?
options: Lack of evidence in either direction
